transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Well, what brings me in is that ever since I stopped working, I just can’t seem to slow down. I’m up and moving from one little job around the house to the next, all day long. It's like I still have a crew waiting on me to get things done, and I just can't sit still.
Over these weeks of staying busy, how would you describe your overall mood - has it felt more anxious and worried, more upbeat or irritable, or fairly normal for you?

My mood? Well, I wouldn't say I feel anxious or worried, really. And I'm not feeling down or overly upbeat either. I'd say my mood has been fairly normal for me. I'm just... busy, you know? But the mood itself is fine.
Would you say this need to stay constantly busy is causing you real distress or getting in the way of things like relaxing, sleeping, or spending time with others?

Well, yeah, it is getting in the way. It's not so much that I'm distressed, but... it's causing problems. My wife has actually had to take over keeping the calendar for us, and she's always having to check behind me to make sure things actually got finished. And outside the house, well, I’ve had to apologize to the folks at the community center and my garden group more than once lately for letting people down or missing things. So, it is definitely affecting my day-to-day life.

Can you tell me approximately how long ago you stopped working, and did this constant need to stay busy begin around that same time or had it been part of how you approached things well before you retired?

Well, I stopped doing handyman work about a year and two months ago. That's when I retired. And to answer your question... that's really when this became a real problem. I guess I was always used to being on the go for my jobs, but it didn't cause issues for me or my wife until after I hung up my tools back then.
Since you retired, have you noticed any feelings of sadness, anxiety, or being lost that seem tied to no longer working, even if your mood feels okay most of the time?

No, I haven't really felt sad or anxious about it. I don't feel lost, either. Like I said, my mood is fine. I'm just always trying to find something to do, but it's not because I'm upset about not working anymore.

Aside from missing appointments or leaving tasks unfinished, have you noticed yourself acting out in ways that break rules or upset others—like being unusually stubborn, argumentative, or disregarding commitments you'd normally respect?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I'm not going around breaking rules or picking fights with anyone. Sure, my wife gets aggravated when I leave a project half-done, but it's not because I'm being stubborn or trying to upset her on purpose. I just... get sidetracked, I guess. But no, I haven't been argumentative or anything like that.
Since you retired about 14 months ago, has this constant need to stay busy stayed pretty much the same the whole time, or has it gotten better or worse at any point?
It's stayed pretty much the same the whole time. I wouldn't say it's gotten any better or worse, really. Just a steady hum of needing to be doing something ever since I stopped working.
Have you noticed any change in your need for sleep lately - for example, feeling rested on much less sleep than usual, or finding it hard to wind down at night?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. My sleep is pretty much the same as it's always been. I definitely still need my regular amount of sleep to feel rested... and I don't really have trouble winding down at night or anything. So, no, no changes there.
Thinking back to when you were a kid or teenager, did you tend to be restless, have trouble sitting still, or have difficulty finishing tasks back then too?

Yeah, definitely. Even way back in... well, grade school, really. I remember my teachers used to say I was bright but scattered. I was the kid who was always losing my pencils or just blurting out answers in class. And they always had to give me reminders to actually finish my work before they'd let me go out for recess. So, yeah, I guess I've always been a bit like that.
